about: The garage's cycle's air, timed by its motion record (data/motion/garage.json, 17 s a round, begun pumped out): the ice the last air carries out as the big door's leaves part, and the fog of the pump-down from 12 s. The same two effects as the airlock and the hangar, by the same rules. Frame: the room's middle on its floor.

effects.name: door_vent
effects.from: footage: S126E014192, STS075-313-022, soyuz-ms22-leak, NTRS-19910011413 (the air the pump leaves (a real airlock's pump stops short of empty and lets the rest out) leaving as the door first opens to the vacuum, its water frozen into fine ice that flies straight out at 16 to 30 m/s with nothing to slow it (NTRS-19910011413's 23 m/s, give or take 30 %), a cone about 14 to 33 degrees either side, under the Moon's 1.62 m/s2; the leaves part from their seam (the west leaf's east edge, 1.27 m east of its middle) at 1 s (data/motion/garage.json big_door_west))

effects.name: door_vent_veil
effects.from: footage: NTRS-19910011413, S126E014192 (the gas itself leaving with the ice, the fine fog of its vapour condensing again, seen as a faint fan of white leaving with the ice at its speed and diverging at its angle (NTRS-19910011413), each puff growing as it spreads so the fan stays one soft band (a vent seen in footage is a soft veil over the sparkling ice, never the ice alone); the leaves part from their seam (the west leaf's east edge, 1.27 m east of its middle) at 1 s (data/motion/garage.json big_door_west))

effects.name: pump_fog
effects.from: footage: normandale-humidity-vacuum, physicsforums-vacuum-chamber-demo (the fog the air makes as the pump draws it down (expanding air cools and its water condenses on the dust in it), forming in the pump's first seconds and gone within seconds as the pressure keeps falling and the air warms again off the walls; the pump runs from 12 s to 17 s of the round (data/motion/garage.json big_door_beacon))

no_light: fog, ice and steam give off no light of their own; the place's lamps light them

footage.how: Measured on each photograph's pixels against a thing of known size in it (named with each source; a typical size where the maker's own was not looked up, so to roughly a third), or read off a report's text. A plume running off the frame bounds a measure on one side only (null). The seconds are the place's own: when its motion record runs the pump and opens the door.

NTRS-19910011413.what: Viereck et al. and Pike et al., the STS-29 water dump observed from the ground (NASA technical reports 19910011413 and 19900037879)
NTRS-19910011413.measured: text: ice particles leave at 23 m/s, give or take 30 %, in a cone traced back to within 1 m of the nozzle, their speed across about a quarter of their speed along (about 14 degrees either side); they flicker as tumbling crystals; the fine fog of vapour condensing again diverges at about the same angle as the trail

S126E014192.what: STS-126's water dump seen from the shuttle's flight deck (NASA)
S126E014192.measured: looked at on the photograph and measured on its pixels: the whole frame dense with fine glittering specks with short streaks, a smooth diffuse glow band under them; nothing of known size in view

STS075-313-022.what: STS-75's waste water dump from the flight deck (NASA)
STS075-313-022.measured: looked at on the photograph and measured on its pixels: a fan of radial streaks about 66 degrees across from where they meet, about 33 degrees either side

normandale-humidity-vacuum.what: Normandale Community College's vacuum-technology article on humidity in vacuum systems: a small cloud forms momentarily as the pressure drops early in roughing, often seen in glass bell jars
normandale-humidity-vacuum.measured: text only: the fog forms in the first moments of the pump-down; no size or duration given

physicsforums-vacuum-chamber-demo.what: a classroom vacuum-chamber demonstration (about a 2-gallon chamber, candle smoke to seed it)
physicsforums-vacuum-chamber-demo.measured: text only: a cloud forms for a few seconds, then disappears; the pressure falls over 50 mbar in the first few seconds

soyuz-ms22-leak.what: Soyuz MS-22's coolant leak at the space station, NASA TV, December 2022
soyuz-ms22-leak.measured: looked at on the photograph and measured on its pixels, against the service module's 2.72 m (234 px): separate specks over at least 450 px, at least 5.2 m, running off the frame
